scenario_description:
Objective: Use a one-afternoon county mobile shredding stop to clear obsolete household paperwork at no cost while preserving current records.
Emerging Need: A general event preview becomes useful only after nearby availability, a helper option, and confirmed drop-off terms align around a short library window.
Decision Context: The saved paper-cleanout note identifies which labeled box is disposable and which active insurance and receipt folders must remain, distinguishing a reversible free drop-off from paid services or over-shredding.
Consequence: Timely use could reduce clutter without changing finances or records; ignoring it leaves the papers where they are, and once the truck leaves the optional benefit is unavailable.

parameter.subject: Saturday mobile shred stop preview for Enid households
parameter.body: County staff expect the mobile consumer-record shred truck to make one Enid stop this afternoon if the route stays on schedule. Final location, hours, and free-service limits will be posted before midday; no reservations are being taken from this preview.

parameter.title: Lunch break near Enid Public Library
parameter.description: Personal break window near the downtown library lot before the afternoon route segment.

parameter.content: I'm passing by your place around 12:30 and then the library after 2. If that free shred truck really opens, I can take one sealed box for you, but text me the exact labeled box so I don't grab current papers.

parameter.subject: Confirmed today: free household document shredding at Enid Library
parameter.body: The mobile shred truck is confirmed for the Enid Public Library west lot today from 2:00 PM to 3:15 PM or until the truck reaches its paper limit. Garfield County households may bring up to two banker boxes of old personal records at no charge. Staff cannot accept boxes after the truck queue closes.

parameter.subject: Enid Library shred truck queue is closed
parameter.body: The mobile shred truck closed the Enid Public Library queue at 3:15 PM after reaching its route limit. No additional household boxes will be accepted today, and the next county consumer-record shredding date has not been scheduled.
